task.title: How to Verify Email Authentication
task.shortdesc: Learn how to check whether a Gmail message is authenticated and recognize indicators of an unauthenticated sender.

taskbody.context:
When an email isn't authenticated, that means Gmail doesn't know if the message is coming from the person who appears to be sending it. If you see a question mark next to the sender's name, the message isn't authenticated. If you see this, be careful about replying or downloading any attachments.
Messages that aren't authenticated aren't necessarily spam. Sometimes authentication doesn't work for real organizations who send mail to big groups, like messages sent to mailing lists.
If you're using an iPhone or iPad, open Gmail on a computer to check the message's authentication details.

step.cmd: Open the email you want to verify.
Below the sender's name, click the Down arrow.

image.alt: Gmail message details showing the down arrow beneath the sender's name.

step.info:
The message is authenticated if you see:
"Mailed-by" header with the domain name, like google.com.
"Signed-by" header with the sending domain. The message isn't authenticated if you see a question mark next to the sender's name. If you see this, be careful about replying or downloading any attachments.
